Veal is baby cow reared in a particular way. Yes, it should be legal to eat veal.

The error you've committed in your question is to assume that treating baby cows in a particular way is "torture". It's not. It's certainly unpleasant for them, but "torture" is something that can only be done to humans: "torture" is when suffering is inflicted with some end (punishment, revenge, extraction of information, etc.) in mind. "Torture" requires a mind capable of understanding that a particular response (emotional, physical or informational) is required. On this interpretation, animals can't be tortured. They can feel pain, but this isn't the same thing.

Veal IS tortured baby cow. Do you disagree?

They're called calves not baby cows, don't try to make emotional appeals. The element of "torture" is the veal crate which has been outlawed in many countries for a long time (as have other elements of the rearing process that are disliked) and in several US states with the whole of the US to phase it out in the near future. There are plenty of farms raising "ethical veal" with none of the traditional veal raising methods so no.
Veal IS NOT tortured baby cow.

Should it be legal to eat veal?

As long as the animal has been treated humanly and hygienically of course it should be legal. If you have a moral objection to eating meat that is your right and you can simply stop eating meat (and using any product which is a by-product of the death of an animal presumably.) Someone who has made that choice DOES NOT have the right to try to shame, disgust or scare others into adopting their moral system.
